name: Norm-Preserving Orthogonal Optimistic Adam
parent_evidence: PCOA was positive at 400, 800 and 1200 updates but reversed to -0.570 dB at 1600 and -0.861 dB at 2400
before the 1600 reversal, mean generator correction/native norm rose from 0.312 at 801-1200 to 0.474 at 1201-1600
entropy-critic predictability reached 0.633 with mean correction/native norm 0.517 at 1201-1600
PCOA confounded directional game-field rotation with radial changes in native Adam displacement magnitude
unsb_object: direction, but not magnitude, of each native G/D/E Adam displacement
mathematical_update: For each player p, let u be the current native Adam displacement, v the previous native displacement, rho=clip(<u,v>/||v||^2,0,1), d=u-v, and d_perp=d-<d,u>u/||u||^2. Form w=u+rho*d_perp and apply u_*=||u||w/||w||. F remains native.
derivation: The component of u-v parallel to u changes step magnitude and caused PCOA to accelerate native update spikes rather than only compensate game rotation.
The orthogonal component is the first-order change in update direction and is therefore the part attributable to phase curvature of the coupled game field.
Projecting the proposal back to the native sphere enforces ||u_*||=||u|| exactly, so the operator cannot accelerate or slow any player's native Adam step.
When consecutive fields are collinear, d_perp=0 and the operator is native even if their magnitudes differ.
When the field is anti-aligned or nonpredictive, rho=0 and the operator is native; every native stationary point remains fixed.
The revision has no tunable strength, window, paired target, endpoint anchor or plain-output target.
identity_condition: first step, rho=0, zero native displacement, or collinear consecutive native displacements
self_null_condition: no predictable angular change exists in the native game field
invariance_property: for every player and update, ||u_*||_2=||u||_2; objectives, endpoint law, Adam moments and fixed points are unchanged
paired_target_proof: the operator uses only current and previous native optimizer displacements
expected_valid_states: predictable angular G-D-E game motion where radial optimism, rather than phase correction itself, caused PCOA reversal
falsification_test: close the coupled-game mechanism if exact norm preservation passes but the 800-step matched trajectory is negative or the independent 2400-step trajectory still reverses
compute_cost: native forward/backward count plus one global dot-product/projection per G/D/E optimizer step
memory_cost: one previous native displacement plus one transient parameter snapshot per G/D/E parameter
allowed_claim: tests whether a norm-neutral phase correction can retain PCOA's early benefit without its radial amplification
forbidden_claims: global convergence for nonconvex three-player UNSB
